findings.title: AC8a removal ticket not created

findings.impact: A required story criterion is only partially met; without an owner and ticket the 2026-12-31 removal (enforced by the removal-date build gate) has no tracked owner, and main builds will start failing on the date with nobody assigned.
findings.recommendation: A human must create the removal ticket (EPM-CDME) listing every deprecated form, the 2026-12-31 removal date and an owner, then reference it from CHANGELOG.md instead of "is owed"; or record an explicit decision that the PR-checklist fallback satisfies AC8a.

decision.rationale: User chose a PR removal checklist instead of a Jira ticket for the 2026-12-31 removals; the release owner tracks it from the PR.

findings.title: Unlocked settings write skips backup bookkeeping
findings.problem: New addClaudeCodeOtlpProject does an unlocked read-modify-write of ~/.claude/settings.json via writeAtomically without refreshing the settings.json.codemie-backup bookkeeping other writers maintain; addCopilotConnectorProject (src/agents/core/copilot-connector-scope.ts) does the same on copilot-connectors.json.
findings.impact: A concurrent edit by Claude Code or another codemie process can be lost, and a later disconnect/restore may work from a stale backup. Reachability of a concurrent writer was unconfirmed.
findings.recommendation: Route addClaudeCodeOtlpProject through the same locked, backup-maintaining writer the other ~/.claude/settings.json writers use, and serialize addCopilotConnectorProject's read-modify-write of copilot-connectors.json the same way.

fix.test: claude-code-otlp-scope.test.ts / copilot-connector-scope.test.ts 'concurrent adds keep every project'

findings.title: BYOK reader and remover disagree on ownership
findings.problem: readVsCodeByokGateway treats any managed provider with at least one loopback model URL as connected, while the remover drops only loopback-only managed providers. A managed provider with mixed loopback and non-loopback model URLs is reported connected but is never removed.
findings.impact: `proxy clients` and doctor report VS Code BYOK connected, and `disconnect --all` counts it disconnected while the config stays. Reachability (a user-edited managed provider with mixed URLs) was unconfirmed.
findings.recommendation: Use one ownership predicate (the remover's loopback-only managed-provider test) in both readVsCodeByokGateway and removeVsCodeLanguageModelsConfigAtPath so clients/doctor/disconnect --all agree with what disconnect removes.
findings.check_notes: readVsCodeByokGateway and the remover both use isCodeMieOwnedProvider (managed provider whose model URLs are all loopback)

fix.change: readVsCodeByokGateway uses the remover's isCodeMieOwnedProvider (loopback-only) predicate
fix.test: vscode.test.ts 'returns null for mixed loopback and non-loopback URLs'

findings.title: disconnect --all silently skips failed checks
findings.problem: disconnectAll uses listConnectedClientTargets, which keeps only connected:true states; readClientTargetStates turns a throwing isConnected into connected:false with an error, so such targets are dropped without a message.
findings.impact: A possibly connected client or connector is not disconnected, the command can print 'Nothing connected.' and exit 0, contradicting AC30's 'reports each'.
findings.recommendation: Read readClientTargetStates() in disconnectAll; for every state with an error print "! <label>: check failed (<error>); not disconnected", add it to result.failed and set exitCode 1, instead of filtering through listConnectedClientTargets.
findings.check_notes: disconnectAll reads readClientTargetStates, reports each failed check as not disconnected, adds it to failed and sets exitCode 1

fix.change: disconnectAll reads readClientTargetStates; a failed check prints '! <label>: check failed (...); not disconnected', is counted failed, exit 1
fix.test: disconnect-all.test.ts 'a target whose connected check failed...'

findings.title: Connect never passes a Next outcome
findings.problem: printNext supports byOutcome, but `proxy connect` and `proxy disconnect` always call it without an outcome, so every target (e.g. --claude-code-otlp vs --claude-desktop, partial --all) gets the same default follow-up.
findings.impact: AC2 ('naming the most relevant follow-up') and the spec's printNext(path, outcome) requirement are partially met; the story's example follow-ups after connecting Claude Code analytics never appear.
findings.recommendation: Derive an outcome from the connected target(s) (e.g. claude-code-otlp, claude-desktop, partial) and call printNext('proxy connect', outcome) / printNext('proxy disconnect', outcome), with byOutcome entries in RELATED, so the follow-up matches the story example.
findings.check_notes: connect passes connectOutcome(opts) and disconnect passes all/stopped; RELATED has byOutcome entries for both

fix.change: connect passes outcome analytics/claude-desktop and disconnect passes all/stopped; RELATED byOutcome entries added
fix.test: connect-wiring.test.ts 'Next line'; related-commands.test.ts 'outcome-specific follow-up'

findings.title: Next line printed after failed commands
findings.problem: printNext never checks process.exitCode, and the connect, disconnect and disconnect --all actions call it unconditionally (index.ts:292, 335, 353), so a 'Next: codemie proxy status' line follows a failed connect, a no-target connect/disconnect that exits 1, and a failed disconnect --all.
findings.impact: AC2 limits the Next line to successful commands; a required criterion is partially met and users are steered onward after a failure.
findings.recommendation: Print the Next line only on success: guard each printNext call (connect, disconnect, disconnect --all) with `if (!process.exitCode)`, or make printNext itself return when process.exitCode is non-zero.
findings.check_notes: printNext returns early when process.exitCode is non-zero (related-commands.ts:147)

fix.change: printNext returns when process.exitCode is non-zero
fix.test: related-commands.test.ts 'prints nothing after a failed command'; connect-wiring.test.ts 'is not printed after a failed connect'

findings.check_notes: connect-wiring tests disconnect --claude-desktop --stop (with and without --stop); disconnect-all test checks 'Failed to stop proxy'

fix.test: connect-wiring.test.ts 'disconnect <target> --stop...'; disconnect-all.test.ts 'a failed stop is reported and exits 1'

findings.title: disconnect --stop stops daemon on usage error
findings.problem: The disconnect action calls stopDaemonAfterDisconnect() whenever opts.stop is set, even when disconnectTargets printed the target list and set exitCode 1 because no target was given.
findings.impact: A usage error (`codemie proxy disconnect --stop`) stops the shared daemon for every connected client.
findings.recommendation: Only stop the daemon when disconnectTargets actually ran a target: e.g. `if (opts.stop && process.exitCode !== 1) await stopDaemonAfterDisconnect();`, or have disconnectTargets return whether any target was selected.
findings.check_notes: disconnectTargets returns ran; the daemon is stopped only when opts.stop && ran; no-target test asserts it is not stopped

fix.change: disconnectTargets returns whether a target ran; --stop only stops the daemon when one did
fix.test: connect-wiring.test.ts 'disconnect --stop with no target is a usage error...'
